Hornet
hôr'nət
n. (a large stinging wasp; the means by which God says He drove out the nations before Israel)
Old English hyrnet, akin to horn. The Hebrew tsirah is a hornet or wasp, and it appears three times, always of God's own agency in the conquest.

Biblical Definition

The promise is given before the crossing: “And I will send hornets before thee, which shall drive out the Hivite, the Canaanite, and the Hittite, from before thee” (Exo 23:28), and repeated: “Moreover the LORD thy God will send the hornet among them, until they that are left, and hide themselves from thee, be destroyed” (Deu 7:20). Joshua, at the end of his life, tells the nation it happened: “And I sent the hornet before you, which drave them out from before you, even the two kings of the Amorites; but not with thy sword, nor with thy bow” (Jos 24:12). That closing clause is the doctrine of the whole conquest in six words. Israel fought real battles with real weapons, and God says the land was not taken by them. Whether the hornets were literal insects or a figure for the terror and confusion God sent ahead of the armies, the point of the verse is unchanged and is stated explicitly: not with thy sword, nor with thy bow. The victory belonged to the LORD, and the men who swung the swords are told so to their faces.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines a hornet as a large strong species of wasp, of a dark brown color, whose sting is severe and irritating.

expand to see more

HORNET, n. [Sax. hyrnet.] A large strong insect of the wasp kind, of a dark brown color.

The sting of the hornet is severe, and the insect is fierce and dangerous.

I will send hornets before thee. Ex. xxiii.

The hornet builds a nest of a substance resembling paper.

Key Scripture

Exo 23:28 — "And I will send hornets before thee, which shall drive out the Hivite, the Canaanite, and the Hittite, from before thee."

Deu 7:20 — "Moreover the LORD thy God will send the hornet among them, until they that are left, and hide themselves from thee, be destroyed."

Jos 24:12 — "And I sent the hornet before you, which drave them out from before you, even the two kings of the Amorites; but not with thy sword, nor with thy bow."

Isa 7:18 — "And it shall come to pass in that day, that the LORD shall hiss for the fly that is in the uttermost part of the rivers of Egypt, and for the bee that is in the land of Assyria."

Modern Corruption

The conquest is discussed only as a moral problem about violence, while Joshua 24:12 insists the decisive agency was not Israel's at all.

expand to see more

Every generation asks about the conquest of Canaan, and the question deserves an answer rather than a shrug. Scripture gives several. The judgment was announced four hundred years in advance and delayed because the iniquity of the Amorites was not yet full. It was judicial, not ethnic: Rahab of Jericho and the Gibeonites were spared, and Israel herself was warned that the land would spew her out for the same sins. And it was limited — a specific commission against specific nations at a specific time, never a general licence, which is why the New Testament church is given no sword at all and told that the weapons of our warfare are not carnal. What Joshua 24:12 adds is the part almost never quoted: God claims the driving out as His own act and denies the sword and bow their credit, which removes the one thing a conquering people always wants, which is glory.

The hornet is worth thinking about as a means. It is not an angel with a flaming sword; it is an insect, or the terror an insect stands for. God's deliverances in Scripture come by small and unglamorous instruments — a stammering shepherd, a boy's sling, a jawbone, a widow's meal barrel, a little maid in Naaman's house, five loaves. Paul draws the rule: God hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty, that no flesh should glory in his presence. Israel entered the land behind hornets, and afterwards had nothing to boast of but the promise of God. A church that wants to see God work should notice what He has generally used, and stop despising the smallness of what is at hand.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew tsirah (H6880), a hornet or wasp; used three times, always of God's sending; with garash (H1644), to drive out, and yarash (H3423), to dispossess.

expand to see more

Hebrew tsirah (H6880) — a hornet; I will send hornets before thee; Exodus 23:28, Deuteronomy 7:20, Joshua 24:12.

Hebrew garash (H1644) — to drive out, to expel; which shall drive out the Hivite, the Canaanite, and the Hittite; Exodus 23:28.

Hebrew yarash (H3423) — to possess by dispossessing; the standing verb of the conquest; Deuteronomy 7:1.

Hebrew chereb (H2719) — a sword; not with thy sword, nor with thy bow; Joshua 24:12.

Hebrew emah (H367) — terror, dread; I will send my fear before thee; Exodus 23:27.

Usage

"“I will send hornets before thee” — the promise, given before the crossing."

"“Until they that are left, and hide themselves from thee, be destroyed” — a judgment long announced."

"“Not with thy sword, nor with thy bow” — the conquest's doctrine in six words."
